entries.title: II Chronicles 21:1
segments: ¶And Jehoshaphat rested with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of David. Then Jehoram his son reigned in his place.

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:2
segments: He had brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azaryahu, Michael, and Shephatiah; all these [were] the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:3
segments: Their father gave them great gifts of silver and gold and precious things, with fortified cities in Judah; but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram, because he [was] the firstborn.

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:4
segments: Now when Jehoram was established over the kingdom of his father, he strengthened himself and killed all his brothers with the sword, and also [others] of the princes of Israel.

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:5
segments: Jehoram [was] thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:6
segments: And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, for he had the daughter of Ahab as a wife; and he did evil in the sight of the LORD.

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:7
segments: Yet the LORD would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that He had made with David, and since He had promised to give a lamp to him and to his sons forever.

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:8
segments: In his days the Edomites revolted against Judah's authority, and made a king over themselves.

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:9
segments: So Jehoram went out with his officers, and all his chariots with him. And he rose by night and attacked the Edomites who had surrounded him and the captains of the chariots.

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:10
segments: Thus Edom has been in revolt against Judah's authority to this day. At that time Libnah revolted against his rule, because he had forsaken the LORD God of his fathers.

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:11
segments: Moreover he made high places in the mountains of Judah, and caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit harlotry, and led Judah astray.

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:12
segments: ¶And a letter came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, Thus says the LORD God of your father David: Because you have not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat your father, or in the ways of Asa king of Judah,

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:13
segments: but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and have made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to play the harlot like the harlotry of the house of Ahab, and also have killed your brothers, those of your father's household, [who were] better than yourself,

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:14
segments: behold, the LORD will strike your people with a serious affliction-your children, your wives, and all your possessions;

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:15
segments: and you [will become] very sick with a disease of your intestines, until your intestines come out by reason of the sickness, day by day.

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:16
segments: Moreover the LORD stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and the Arabians who [were] near the Ethiopians.

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:17
segments: And they came up into Judah and invaded it, and carried away all the possessions that were found in the king's house, and also his sons and his wives, so that there was not a son left to him except Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:18
segments: After all this the LORD struck him in his intestines with an incurable disease.

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:19
segments: Then it happened in the course of time, after the end of two years, that his intestines came out because of his sickness; so he died in severe pain. And his people made no burning for him, like the burning for his fathers.

entries.title: II Chronicles 21:20
segments: He was thirty-two years old when he became king. He reigned in Jerusalem eight years and, to no one's sorrow, departed. However they buried him in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
